# Make videos with the crew

You get watermarked clips in `.agent-out/studio/<studio>/`, each with the crew's verdicts before and after the render (`panel.json`), the words to post (`post.txt`) and the frames the viewer looked at. `docs/agents/STUDIO.md` has a worked example; `AGENTS.md` is the contract.

## The rules

- Every clip is a free visitor's render and carries the watermark. Never install or use a licence, never the TEST key: a clip the page reports clean is refused.
- The tools write only under `.agent-out/`. You write no file and edit nothing in the repository for a video.
- The rules overrule every role, you included: a clip that fails a gate is never kept, evidence is the dossier's keys, fixes come from the fixed list, one fix round and never a second.
- A verdict never deletes a clip. Never push and never post: the owner approves every post.
- Other creators' titles and names never go into a brief, a verdict or a post.

## Who plays which role

The same model plays every role, each in a fresh context: hand each brief to its subagent, one brief per subagent run. The clarity check and the picker are code.

| Role | Subagent | The panel asks for it | Its job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| researcher | `jbl-researcher` | when the panel was started with "research":"live" | the research digest in at most five pieces of advice, each with its lever and its strength |
| brainstormer | `jbl-brainstormer` | for an open request (a review started with "request" and no plan) | different clips for an open request, each a ready template on one of its modes |
| skeptic | `jbl-skeptic` | on each candidate before the render | a clip's one idea and at most three objections, each citing the dossier's keys; never a fix |
| viewer | `jbl-viewer` | on each rendered clip after the render (and before it at Thorough depth) | what a stranger thinks a clip is about, from what is on screen alone |
| reviewer | `jbl-reviewer` | where something is in doubt, before and after the render (on every clip at Thorough depth) | keep, fix or drop, every confirmed objection and misread answered, fixes from the fixed list |
| producer | `jbl-producer` | once the panel has picked the clips to keep | the words around the kept clips: a file name, a title, a caption ending on one question, hashtags; the hook as drawn |

The subagents reach the panel through `mcp__jumpingballs-agent__review`, the project's MCP server's review tool: approve the server (`/mcp`) first. You drive the loop with the CLI (`npm run -s agent -- <tool> --json '{…}'`) or the same MCP tools.

## The loop

1. `npm run -s agent -- research --json '{}'`: the research brief, at most five pieces of advice; a weak finding is weak. When the trend summary is stale, `inspire` on a template's theme words refreshes the evidence first.
2. `npm run -s agent -- templates --json '{}'`: the ready templates. The battle family (Fight League names third-party characters) only when the owner asks for it.
3. `npm run -s agent -- plan --json '{"template":"<id>","count":3,"platform":"<reels|tiktok|shorts>","world":{"width":800,"height":450},"studio":"<studio>"}'`: plan for the platform asked for (default reels), in the page's world. For an open request skip the plan: the review starts with `"request"` and the brainstormer pitches.
4. `npm run -s agent -- review --json '{"studio":"<studio>","separation":"contexts"}'` starts the panel (add `"request"`, `"wanted"`, `"platform"` and `"world":{"width":800,"height":450}` for an open request, so its ideas are planned for that platform in the page's world; `"depth":"thorough"` to ask every role). While its `status` is "call": hand `next.role`'s subagent the arguments `{"studio":"<studio>"}` and `next.clip`, then call `npm run -s agent -- review --json '{"studio":"<studio>"}'` again for the next brief. Never answer a brief yourself while the subagents run.
5. `npm run -s agent -- render --json '{"plan":".agent-out/studio/<studio>/plan.json","clip":"<a kept clip>"}'` for each clip the decision keeps: watermarked, with its melody and its sheets.
6. `npm run -s agent -- review --json '{"studio":"<studio>","stage":"post"}'`: the viewer's look at each rendered clip and the reviewer where the read, the rules or the facts disagree. The panel after the render is its own: every call of it keeps `"stage":"post"`, your re-fetches for the next brief as well as the subagents' arguments (a call without it reaches the finished panel before the render). The viewer looks at the clip's sheet.png and hook-sheet.png itself. A fix the reviewer offers there: `npm run -s agent -- render --json '{"plan":".agent-out/studio/<studio>/plan.json","clip":"<the clip>","fixed":true}'` makes it as a clip of its own (`<clip>-fixed`; the review's `fixed` lists the calls), and the panel after the render looks at it on its next call.
7. Hand over the studio folder: the clips, panel.json and post.txt; say which clips were kept or dropped and why, which fixes were applied or offered, and that the roles ran in separate contexts (or that they did not).

Without subagents (the MCP server not approved, or a client without them), play each role yourself through the CLI, one brief at a time, and leave `separation` at its default: the record then says the roles shared one context.

## The role eval

Only when the owner asks for it: `npm run -s agent -- review --json '{"studio":"eval-<name>","fixture":true,"separation":"contexts"}'` asks the eval's briefs on the fixture corpus (the cold viewer's first); hand each to its subagent with `"fixture":true` in its arguments, as in the loop. When the status is "done", `npm run crew:fixtures -- --record eval-<name> --model <the model's id>` keeps the run and writes its tables into `docs/agents/CREW-EVAL.md`. Say in the hand-over that one model played every role, and which.
